summary.text: 南 is attested for “south” in Shang inscriptions. Its early graph may picture an object, but proposals identifying it as an instrument, a house front, or a covered vessel remain disputed.

formation.text: The early graph is treated as pictographic in competing proposals, but its referent is unsettled: it has been read as a hanging percussion instrument, a house front, or a covered vessel with a plant-like feature. Separately, the received Shuowen analysis says the graph is formed from 𣎵 and the phonetic 𢆉; the available evidence does not independently verify that historical sound relation.

components.text: In one disputed analysis, the whole early graph depicts a hanging percussion instrument; other accounts identify it as a house front or a covered vessel. The evidence does not establish which object, if any, the graph depicts.
In the received Shuowen account, 𣎵 is the semantic component. This is a historical dictionary analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original pictorial source.
The received Shuowen account identifies 𢆉 as phonetic, but the historical sound relationship is not independently verified here.

sound_limitation.text: The current Mandarin readings rěn and nán can be compared, but this modern pair does not establish that 𢆉 had a phonetic role in 南 historically.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are recorded as rěn for 𢆉 and nán for 南; this comparison documents modern readings only.

history.text: Oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, and seal forms are reported, and the received dictionary tradition also records 𡴖 as an ancient form. The available accounts do not establish a continuous graphic sequence from the Shang forms to the later character.

Shang inscriptions report 南 for the direction, in the ancestor name 南庚, and for a sacrificial item. The suggestion that an object sign was reused for “south” because the words sounded alike is unverified: the proposed object, its ancient name, and its pronunciation are unresolved, and the inscriptions do not establish which use came first.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent remains disputed among instrument, house-front, covered-vessel, and other proposals. A proposed lexical link between “south” and a belly or front-of-body word concerns the spoken word’s history; it does not establish the graph’s formation or a semantic path.
The exact earliest inscription and the order of the reported Shang uses are unresolved; a continuous graphic derivation is also not established.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone inscriptions; exact earliest specimen date unresolved
senses.text: 南 is attested for the direction “south” in Shang oracle-bone inscriptions. This is an early documented use, not proof that “south” was the graph’s original meaning.
南 is also used for a southern part; its date relative to the directional sense is unresolved.
南 is also used to mean southward; its date relative to the directional sense is unresolved.

limitations.text: The reported ancestor-name and sacrificial-item uses do not establish separate character senses or a chronology among the Shang uses.

Instrument-name borrowing is a proposal, not a verified explanation: the proposed instrument’s identity, ancient name, and pronunciation are unresolved, and the reported Shang uses do not establish that the directional word was borrowed from its name.
The proposed lexical link between “south” and a belly or front-of-body word does not establish a semantic development.

overview.text: 南 means “south,” a use attested in Shang inscriptions. One proposal says an early object sign was reused for “south” because the words sounded alike or similar, but the object, its name, and the sound match remain unresolved.

components.text: One disputed proposal reads the whole early graph as an object picture; proposed objects include an instrument, a house front, and a covered vessel.
The received Shuowen account treats 𣎵 as contributing meaning; this is a historical analysis, not a settled account of the graph’s origin.
The received Shuowen account calls 𢆉 a sound element, but its present-day reading alone does not prove that historical role.

relationships.text: This disputed analysis treats the whole early graph as a picture of an object, while competing interpretations identify different objects.
The received Shuowen analysis assigns 𣎵 a semantic role within 南; this historical dictionary account is not independent confirmation of the graph’s original formation.
The received Shuowen analysis calls 𢆉 phonetic. Its current Mandarin reading rěn can be compared with 南 nán, but this modern pair does not verify the proposed historical phonetic relation.
